title: Kaleidoscope batch tuner: continuous workload profiler and safe parameter annealer
creator: Anita Shah
description:
Summary:
Kaleidoscope is a new continuous batching parameter tuner that synthesizes workload profiles, heuristic scoring, and a conservative annealing strategy to recommend batching and KV-caching configs for production routes. Goal is to reduce per-token cost by 8–20% on compatible workloads while preserving latency and p99 SLOs.

Background and motivation:
We have many single-shot and chat workloads with diverse sequence-length distributions and arrival patterns. Existing static heuristics and one-off autotunes produce improvements but require manual review and are brittle when traffic patterns shift. Kaleidoscope combines a rolling workload census (per-route, per-customer), a lightweight fingerprinting layer, and a constrained optimizer that proposes safe parameter deltas (batch-size, max-concurrency, prefix-cache TTLs, coalescing window) and automates a guarded rollout (shadow -> small canary -> staged ramp -> full apply) with automatic rollback on safety signals.

What this ticket covers:
1) Implement continuous workload profiler agent that emits histogram fingerprints (sequence length, token arrival ISI, KV cache hit-rate estimate, prompt size buckets) to the metrics pipeline.
2) Build heuristic scorer that converts profiles into candidate parameter deltas with an explainable priority score (cost delta vs risk). Heuristics include: latency sensitivity metric, tail-sway factor, warm-cache multiplier, and transient-burst detection.
3) Add annealing controller that proposes incremental changes and schedules safe-apply steps (shadow apply for 2h, canary 1% traffic for 1h, ramp to 10% for 2h, then 100%) with automated rollback gates.
4) Integrate with Console rollout APIs and add telemetry panels + alerts.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Global model quantization recommendations (follow-on project).
- Dedicated-only autoscaler integration (separate ENG project).

Design highlights and rationale:
- Conservative deltas: limit batch_size increase to at most +50% per apply, concurrency to +30%, and coalescing window to +25% absolute to avoid head-of-queue latency regressions.
- Shadow simulation: apply candidate parameters in the runtime request path as a passive branch that records expected cost and latency without affecting responses. Use sampled prefix traces to predict tail behavior.
- Heuristic ensemble: combine rule-based signals with a light-weight cost model that uses observed tokenization distributions and recent KV-hit heuristics. Rule-based overrides prevent changes when p95/p99 are close to SLO threshold or when error rate > baseline*1.1.
- Explainability: each recommendation includes the top 3 contributing signals and an expected cost delta range; exposed in the Console as a short justification for SRE/PM review.

Acceptance criteria:
- Profiler emits histograms and fingerprints for 90% of production routes with <1% additional CPU overhead on collector agents.
- Heuristic scorer generates recommendations for >30% of eligible routes in the pilot group and shows simulated cost savings in shadow mode.
- Rollout controller performs shadow -> canary -> ramp as configured; automatic rollback triggers on: p99 increase >10% absolute, error-rate increase >0.5pp, or drop in throughput >8% for 5m.
- Console shows a Kaleidoscope dashboard with per-route recommendation cards, simulate vs observed charts, and a one-click approve/reject for manual override.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: Profiler agent prototype + metrics schema (histograms, fingerprint id). Instrument two low-risk routes for pilot.
- Week 2: Heuristic scorer service (stateless) with REST endpoint and local sim runner; initial ruleset v0.1.
- Week 3: Shadow simulator integrated into runtime, store simulation metrics in temp-prometheus namespace.
- Week 4: Rollout controller + Console UI skeleton, wiring the approval flow.
- Week 5: Pilot canary for 1% traffic across 6 routes; evaluate for 72h.

Testing and telemetry plan:
- Unit tests for scorer and annealer: target 85% coverage.
- E2E shadow vs real compare tests using recorded traces to validate simulation accuracy within ±8% for p50/p95 cost estimates.
- Dashboard: grafana/redwood/kaleidoscope and alerting rule IDs: RBW-KALE-001 (p99 regression), RBW-KALE-002 (error rate spike), RBW-KALE-003 (apply-failure).
- Post-apply evaluation job to run automatically 24h after full apply and produce a mutation report (latency, error rate, cost delta).

Safety and rollback strategy:
- Shadow apply must succeed with no request path changes before any canary.
- Canary limited to 1% traffic and pinned to low-risk zones/nodes.
- Automated rollback: detect rule violations and immediately flip config to previous parameters; notify on-call and create incident ticket with attached mutation report and trace examples.
- Manual kill switch in Console to abort ongoing rollouts and revert live configs.

Open questions / risks:
- How to best estimate KV cache warmup effect for ephemeral routes? Proposal: track route-level warm-cache multiplier from shadow runs and require a minimum of 4h observed warm-cache signal before larger deltas.
- Cross-route interference: increasing batch sizes on many routes simultaneously could hurt shared GPU latency. Mitigation: global coordinator keeps an active change budget per cluster (max aggregate batch increase %).
- Regulatory: customers with private deployments may want opt-out; add config flag at the org level.

Dependencies and related work:
- Depends on ENG-7421 for baseline batching telemetry schema (already merged).
- Console work: PM-1208 (rollouts API) and DES-412 (recommendation card UI).

updates: 2026-02-26: Spike complete for fingerprint schema. Profiler prototype emits histograms to metrics ingestion (PR #38). Noticed collectors add ~0.6% CPU on staging agents.

2026-03-03: Heuristic scorer v0.1 tested offline against 7 days of traces. Scorer flagged 28% of routes as candidates; simulated median cost delta 11%. Added rule to block routes with p99 within 5% of SLO.

2026-03-08: Shadow integration merged into runtime (PR #2017). Shadow branches record expected latency and KV-hit proxies to temp namespace. Ran 48h shadow on 4 routes; simulated cost was within 7% of observed.
2026-03-11: Rollout controller basic flow implemented. Initial canary plan scheduled for 2026-03-16 on pilot cohort. Need Console team to wire approve button (DES-412 blocker).
2026-03-12: Security review requested for pilot (security_review_required = true). Added opt-out flag for orgs; legal to review customer communications.
